subject: Pilot runway: surge protection vs conversion bonus decision
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Dunne <alex.dunne@horizonhealth.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-22T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot runway: surge protection vs conversion bonus decision

Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We ran through the usage during the trial and I pulled together two options for closing the gap as you scale your evaluation into production: one focused on surge insurance (capacity + burst protection) and one that leans on a conversion bonus (a one-time credit tied to an early commit). I attached a short pricing matrix that lays out the math for both approaches.

TL;DR options:
- Surge insurance: one-time fee that guarantees a sustained burst pool for the remaining trial period (covers up to 3x baseline concurrency for 30 days) + priority routing. This protects you from throttling and keeps latency SLOs.
- Conversion bonus: if Horizon signs an LOI for Dedicated capacity within 30 days of pilot end, we’ll apply a one-time credit (percentage of billed pilot overrun) and a preferential committed rate for Q1 post-conversion.

Questions for you:
1) Which is more valuable to the Horizon engineering team — predictable access during the last push, or a financial incentive to convert now?
2) Do you have an internal budget we should aim for for a short-term surge insurance buy?

I’ve cc’d Ben to outline the pricing flexibility. If it helps, we can combine both: a reduced surge fee plus a smaller conversion credit if Horizon commits inside 45 days.

Attachments: pilot_pricing_matrix_v3.pdf (1 page summary), redwood_pilot_terms.docx (pilot addendum draft)

Next step suggestion: 30-minute call today or tomorrow to pick the path and I’ll draft an addendum.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

From: Alex Dunne <alex.dunne@horizonhealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@horizonhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-22T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot runway: surge protection vs conversion bonus decision

Thanks Laura — helpful summary and thanks for the matrix. Two quick points from our side:

1) Engineering priority: predictability. We had a spike on Wed that caused queued inference for a handful of clinical flows; minimizing that risk for the final two weeks is the priority.
2) Budget: we have a limited eval budget and can stretch ~USD 12k for a short-term insurance buy, but any material incentive to commit would need to sit in the leadership approval queue (longer lead time).

Priya and I discussed the combined approach you mentioned (reduced surge fee + smaller conversion credit) — that sounds workable, provided the surge protection covers sustained bursts and there’s clear telemetry we can use to justify the buy internally. Can you outline what telemetry/reporting is included with the surge insurance?

Also — if we do a conversion bonus, what’s the typical horizon for the preferential rate? How long does that pricing hold?

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call this afternoon at 3pm PT if that works for you.

—Alex
Alex Dunne
Director of Platform Engineering, Horizon Health
alex.dunne@horizonhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Dunne <alex.dunne@horizonhealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-07-22T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot runway: surge protection vs conversion bonus decision

Alex — quick follow from our side on telemetry and commercial windows:

Telemetry that comes with the surge insurance package:
- Real-time token-level throughput dashboard (per-route breakdown)
- Burst utilization heatmap (1m/5m/1h buckets)
- Incident traces for any throttling events + automated sampling of affected requests for post-mortem
- Cost/latency delta report comparing baseline vs burst windows

Commercial windows on conversion bonus:
- Preferential committed rate applies for the first 90 days after go-live (to let you ramp), with the option to extend pricing via a 6-month commitment addendum at the same rate if signed within 60 days of conversion.
- Conversion credit (the one-time credit) can be applied against the first invoice after conversion.

About pricing flexibility: for Horizon I can offer a compressed combined package given the clinical throughput use-case:
- Surge insurance (reduced): USD 9,500 for 30 days (baseline + 2.5x burst pool) — includes the telemetry above and a guaranteed response SLA for burst windows.
- Conversion credit: 20% of the billed overrun up to USD 15,000 if LOI signed within 45 days.

This keeps the surge fee inside your stated stretch budget and gives leadership a tangible incentive if they move quickly. 

If you want, I’ll sketch this into the addendum and route for approvals. Laura — if you’re comfortable with this framing I’ll prepare the legal hook-ups and the pricing line items.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Priya Singh <priya.singh@horizonhealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Dunne <alex.dunne@horizonhealth.com>
Date: 2027-07-22T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot runway: surge protection vs conversion bonus decision

Ben / Laura — thanks, that structure is much clearer and the pricing hits our budget expectations. A few operational asks before we greenlight the reduced surge buy: 

1) Can you add a clause that explicitly states what constitutes a "burst" event in the dashboard (thresholds and measurement window)?
2) We need the telemetry export (CSV/JSON) available daily for our internal compliance review — can that be automated?
3) On the conversion credit, can the credit be applied to either the first invoice or the implementation professional services invoice (we often separate those)?

If you can confirm these three points we’ll sign the short addendum and proceed with the USD 9,500 surge insurance buy today. We can loop procurement for the LOI separately.

—Priya
